paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of it: Christ set us free, so STAND in that freedom (Gal 5:1). Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, where some people are pushing the believers toward circumcision and the law. He tells them plainly that trying to be justified by the law cuts a person off from Christ and from grace (Gal 5:2-4). Our hope comes another way: "by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Gal 5:5).

So what counts? Paul says, "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Gal 5:6). The Galatians were running so well, and somebody got in their way, and Paul says that kind of persuasion doesn't come from the One who calls them (Gal 5:7-8). Then he reaches into MY kitchen: "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Gal 5:9). I think Paul is saying a little bad teaching doesn't stay little, so don't let it near the batch.

But freedom isn't a license to do whatever you want. Paul says they were called to freedom, so "serve one another in love" (Gal 5:13). The entire law is fulfilled in "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Gal 5:14). And if they keep on biting and devouring one another, he warns they will be consumed by one another (Gal 5:15). Christ freed you, friend, so use that freedom to love somebody today.
